description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of large language models, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of SepLLM and StrmLLM, as evaluated in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000, and uses a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick marks at 0.1 intervals, also on a linear scale. Six distinct lines are plotted: “Vanilla” (purple, solid line) starts at approximately 3.35 and steadily declines to about 2.52; “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid) begins near 3.35 and decreases to roughly 2.62; “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid) starts at ~3.3 and ends at ~2.54; “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid) begins at ~3.28 and ends at ~2.53; “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid) starts at ~3.25 and ends at ~2.51; and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid) begins at ~3.3 and ends at ~2.58. All lines exhibit a steep initial drop in loss within the first 20,000 iterations, followed by a slower, more gradual decline toward convergence. The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” variant consistently achieves the lowest loss across most of the training trajectory, while “StrmLLM (n=64)” maintains the highest loss after the initial iterations.
